findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Name the actor for the countersign step explicitly, for example the manager countersigns the employee's request within two business days, and keep every sentence in the paragraph addressed to the same reader.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the reader directly as you for submitting and tracking the request, then inserts an imperative, Countersign the employee request, with no stated actor, so the reader cannot tell whether this you is being asked to countersign the request or whether that action belongs to a different reader entirely, such as the approving manager.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the item or amount being reimbursed and use it in all three sentences.
findings.violation: Three consecutive sentences use three different terms, the stipend item, the reimbursable item, and the covered purchase amount, for what appears to be the single item or amount the employee is requesting reimbursement for, with no defined-terms signal that the three phrases mean the same thing, so a reader cannot tell whether these are one concept or three.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing. The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request.
findings.fix: Reorder the paragraphs so the review-before-submitting step comes before the sign-off and final-processing step, in the order the employee actually experiences them.
findings.violation: The second paragraph states that the request has already moved to final processing and that the employee already received a confirmation email once processing finishes, and the third paragraph, introduced with Then as if it were the next step, describes the employee reviewing a summary before submitting the final request, a step that logically precedes final processing, so the two paragraphs cannot be placed on one timeline and a reader cannot tell in what order these events actually happen.

findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. [...] Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Move the countersigning detail and the Request Steps content into or immediately after How to Apply, in the order the reader actually performs them.
findings.location: Terminology Notes and Request Steps sections
findings.violation: Information a reader needs while actually applying, who signs off on the request and the full step sequence, is split across Terminology Notes and Request Steps, which sit after Required Documentation, Reimbursement Amounts, and Restrictions and Exceptions, sections that only make sense once a request has already been approved and paid, rather than appearing near or inside How to Apply where the reader would need them.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the sentences unrelated to stipend program coordination, or move each to a section its own topic actually belongs to.
findings.violation: A reader who reads only the section's first and last sentences, about the benefits team coordinating requests and the office coffee budget, cannot state what the section is about, because its four sentences move through stipend coordination, an unrelated travel-expense audit, federal remote-work guidance, and the coffee budget, three unrelated themes with nothing connecting them to the section's heading or to each other.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Rewrite the section around one running topic, stipend program coordination, and drop or relocate sentences whose subject does not connect to it.
findings.violation: Each of the section's four sentences opens with a new subject, the benefits team, a separate audit, federal guidance, the office coffee budget, and no sentence's subject picks up the topic the sentence before it just established, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary instead of following one running topic.

findings.evidence: You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year.
findings.fix: Pick one address mode, second person throughout or third person throughout, and apply it consistently across every section.
findings.violation: This section and Terminology Notes address the reader directly as you and refer to the policy owner as we, while every other section refers to the reader in the third person as employees or the employee, so the document does not consistently establish who its single intended reader is.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Rewrite with the employee as the subject and the actual actions as the sentence's main verbs, for example the employee completes the request by confirming eligibility and uploading a receipt.
findings.violation: The sentence's subject, completing the request, is an abstract nominalized process standing in for the employee, who is the one actually confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt and who could be named as the subject instead.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Restate every item in the series with the same grammatical form.
findings.violation: The series' 2 items mix grammatical forms (gerund, other) at their head words instead of sharing one form.
